result:
Round 218 is planned and handed to A: **PERF-16a**, which moves the Studio lab's MP3 export from ffmpeg.wasm to mediabunny with the LAME encoder. Decision: **CONTINUE**.

**Round 217:** C passed all 8 rows with real browser checks and found 0 bugs. Gate 217 published `8873ece`. PERF-1b-ii and PERF-1b are now done in the backlog. Gate 217's code review also covered the four late perf-spec changes, so that open item is closed. Its four Low findings went to `deferred_low_polish`. The regression round is not due until 2026-10-30.

**Dependencies:** I filed `root-deps-request.json` asking for `mediabunny@1.62.1` and `@mediabunny/mp3-encoder@1.62.1`. Both are on the allowlist, and I checked they exist on npm under MPL-2.0. Root installs them at the start of the next job, before A begins. The round's baseline is that install commit sitting directly on `8873ece`. If the commit or the package is missing, A stops without changing anything. I have not asked to remove `@ffmpeg/*` yet: the old `/studio/:productId` path still imports it, so removing it now would break the build.

**What A changes (4 files plus a new doc 170, everything else frozen):**
- `mp3-encoder.client.ts` is rewritten. Its exported functions keep the same names and signatures, so the export logic and the six test files that mock this module don't change.
- LAME is always used, at fixed 320 kbps CBR (constant bitrate), the same format Ableton Live 12 exports (manual §5.1.3.3). This keeps the file identical across browsers.
- Cancel stops any running encode, and an encoder left over from before a reset refuses new work.
- The WAV is read in pieces, so the whole file is never copied into memory.
- Nothing loads from an outside host any more.
- Three dialog strings that are now false (CDN, ~31 MB, ffmpeg.wasm) are replaced with shorter ones.
- Nine unit test rows cover this. One checks that no other file imports mediabunny, so it can't end up in the page's initial load.

**What C checks in the browser:**
- A real MP3 at both screen sizes: each audio frame's format (320 kbps, 48 kHz, stereo), the length, and loudness against the WAV.
- No requests to outside hosts, and no encoder worker left running after cancel.
- WAV + MP3 together, and a range MP3.
- The dialog wording.
- On the production build, the encoder is at most 1 MiB compressed and loads only on MP3 export.
- One run of the resources performance test.
- The sign-in guard still blocks anonymous access, and WAV export still works.

The old `/studio/:productId` path can't be tested in the cloud because it needs the backend.

**After this round:** OSS-LIC is round 219 (third-party licence notices and a GPL/AGPL check), unless the regression round is due by then. PERF-16b comes after it: the old path moves to the same encoder, then `@ffmpeg/*` is removed. Removing it also needs a one-line root grant for `vite.config.ts`.

The advisor was available and I consulted it twice, as well as tech-lead and performance-optimizer as the PERF rule requires. I adopted their advice, including the advisor's last three fixes that prevent false C failures. App source is untouched and the store tree is clean.
